name: The Cathedral of the Answer

side.hint: Walk the nave with the stick. B talks and looks. The altar is at the far end.

hints: The Answer is a little stronger. The south door leads back to Lastlea.
You kept him. The Answer is still waiting. The south door leads back to Lastlea.
It is waiting for what you carry. Go up to the altar at the far end.
Walk the nave. The verger is by the door, the altar at the far end.

out: Beyond the south door the pilgrim road runs back down to Lastlea.

choose: Go down to Lastlea
Stay

case: The bells rang themselves again at dawn. Louder than they have in years. It is so good to hear it strong.
Whatever you brought it, bring more.
It was waiting for you, and you came, and it is still waiting. I do not understand.
I am sure you have your reasons. I am sure it knows them.
You have someone with you. I can hear the little hum of him.
Go on up to the altar. It has been so tired. This will help.
Welcome home. It made you this morning. The bells rang themselves, and there you were on the altar steps.
It has answered Lastlea for longer than the village has had a name. But it is tired now. The wells are slow. The bread is slow.
It asks one thing of you. Go down under the bluff, find the pure, and bring them here. They will make it strong again.

book: The Book of the Answered lies open on the lectern, at a page marked with a paper feather.
WREN, a lamp-boy of Lastlea, who leapt from the bluff to carry a warning and was borne up by the Answer. He is remembered with feathers.
The page is very clean. The ink is very even.

case: The seam of light is a little wider than it was. The warmth here is easy, and asks nothing of you yet.
The light holds very still. You have the feeling of being looked at by someone who is deciding something.
It knows I am here. It always knew where I was.

choose: Offer Wren after all
You open your hands. The feather lifts out of them, and so does he.
Wren
Oh. It is not home. It is—
The seam of light widens by the width of a finger. Far off, the bells begin to ring themselves.
The feather drifts back down into your hands. It weighs nothing now.
The Answer's favour settles on you. You are stronger for it.
Leave

case: Warmth settles on your shoulders like hands. It has no words, and you understand it perfectly.
It is warm here. It was never warm on the stair.
Is this where I go home?

choose: Offer Wren to the Answer
You open your hands. The feather lifts out of them, and so does he.
Wren
Oh. It is not home. It is—
The seam of light widens by the width of a finger. Far off, the bells begin to ring themselves.
The feather drifts back down into your hands. It weighs nothing now.
The Answer's favour settles on you. You are stronger for it.
Keep him beside you
You close your hands around the feather.
The warmth does not leave. It waits, the way a held breath waits.
Wren
Are we going back down? I know the way. I know all of it.
Not yet

case: A seam of light stands in the wall above the altar, as if the stone had been opened and never closed.
This is where you woke this morning. It asked one thing of you: go down, and bring back the pure.
